## Proof

The Structural Stress Factor for module $n$ is $n^2 - 1 = (n-1)(n+1)$. We need this to equal the product of exactly 3 distinct primes (i.e., $n^2-1 = pqr$ with $p<q<r$ all prime, and no higher prime powers).

I check each $n$ starting from 1, factoring $n^2-1$:

|-----|---------|---------------|-------------------|
| 2 | 3 | 3 | no (1 prime) |
| 3 | 8 | $2^3$ | no |
| 4 | 15 | $3\cdot5$ | no (2 primes) |
| 5 | 24 | $2^3\cdot3$ | no |
| 6 | 35 | $5\cdot7$ | no |
| 7 | 48 | $2^4\cdot3$ | no |
| 8 | 63 | $3^2\cdot7$ | no |
| 9 | 80 | $2^4\cdot5$ | no |
| 10 | 99 | $3^2\cdot11$ | no |
| 11 | 120 | $2^3\cdot3\cdot5$ | no (powers) |
| 12 | 143 | $11\cdot13$ | no (2 primes) |
| 13 | 168 | $2^3\cdot3\cdot7$ | no |
| **14** | **195** | $3\cdot5\cdot13$ | **yes ✓** |
| 15 | 224 | $2^5\cdot7$ | no |
| **16** | **255** | $3\cdot5\cdot17$ | **yes ✓** |
| 17 | 288 | $2^5\cdot3^2$ | no |
| 18 | 323 | $17\cdot19$ | no (2 primes) |
| 19 | 360 | $2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5$ | no |
| **20** | **399** | $3\cdot7\cdot19$ | **yes ✓** |
| 21 | 440 | $2^3\cdot5\cdot11$ | no |
| **22** | **483** | $3\cdot7\cdot23$ | **yes ✓** |
| 23 | 528 | $2^4\cdot3\cdot11$ | no |
| 24 | 575 | $5^2\cdot23$ | no |
| 25 | 624 | $2^4\cdot3\cdot13$ | no |
| 26 | 675 | $3^3\cdot5^2$ | no |
| 27 | 728 | $2^3\cdot7\cdot13$ | no |
| 28 | 783 | $3^3\cdot29$ | no |
| 29 | 840 | $2^3\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7$ | no (4 primes) |
| 30 | 899 | $29\cdot31$ | no (2 primes) |
| 31 | 960 | $2^6\cdot3\cdot5$ | no |
| **32** | **1023** | $3\cdot11\cdot31$ | **yes ✓** |

The first 5 Stable Modules are $n = 14, 16, 20, 22, 32$.

Verification of each:
- $14^2-1 = 195 = 3\times5\times13$ ✓
- $16^2-1 = 255 = 3\times5\times17$ ✓
- $20^2-1 = 399 = 3\times7\times19$ ✓
- $22^2-1 = 483 = 3\times7\times23$ ✓
- $32^2-1 = 1023 = 3\times11\times31$ ✓

The sum is:
$$14 + 16 + 20 + 22 + 32 = 104$$
